chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from one of his companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

The remaining upon the deed is more difficult than the deed itself. He said, 'And what is the remaining upon the deed?' He said, 'The man maintains relationships by helping (a relative) and he spends an expenditure for the Sake of Allah Alone, there being no associates for Him, so a secretive good deed is Recorded for him. Then he mentions it and it gets Deleted, and an open good deed is Recorded for him. Then he mentions it (again), and a showing-off is Recorded for him'.

key_terms.الْإِبْقَاءُ عَلَى الْعَمَلِ: Remaining upon the deed / Maintaining consistency in action
key_terms.رِيَاءٌ: Showing off / Performing deeds for public display

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between secret charity and showing off (riya) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights that sustaining sincerity (ikhlas) is more arduous than the initial act of worship, illustrating the fragility of spiritual reward through the gradual erosion of secret charity into public recognition and finally to riya (showing off). This hadith is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the dynamic nature of deeds, where the same action can shift from pure worship to diminished reward based on the believer's awareness and disclosure. It underscores the scholarly emphasis on guarding the heart against the subtle incursions of self-praise even after the deed is completed.
